I closed that mouth, source of unnecessary remarks, with my fist.

Privately, I did not entirely disagree.

On a park bench, of all places, the man sat with his back perfectly straight. Yet it did not look stiff. Probably he had sat that way for so long that it was quite natural.

Was that why he was tall?

...Then was I short because I slouched? Arre. Possible. An unpleasantly possible possibility.

A substantial lump stood on his forehead. Cool it, and probably it would soon heal. Still, if that lump were on my head, forgiving without complaint would be beyond me.

His generosity really was something.

Of course he could not.

Rokuhara, the strongest force in Yamato, controlled all the country's warriors. Nobody could defy it.

If there was one exception—

That was the unidentified warrior called Silver Star. The silver killer. A monster that made prey even of Rokuhara.

Believe the rumors slipping past the Shogunate's information controls, and it had wiped out an entire company of Rokuhara warriors.

Alone.

True or not, I did not know. But where Silver Star was concerned, Rokuhara's usual arrogant leisure vanished. One unreliable lead, and investigators ran this way; another, that way.

Rokuhara itself seemed frightened.

Some among the anti-Shogunate groups scattered through Yamato were said to treat Silver Star as a hero because of this.

...Civilians were among the victims, too.

Silver Star, Rain of Death.

We did not know its true nature. But if one warrior really brushed Rokuhara aside like that, then unquestionably it was this world's <ruby>strongest single being<rt>top one</rt></ruby>.

Nobody could win.

Winning against it was not possible.
